67.1.3.meaning: Shumm: men with high-bridged noses, the proud and noble.

67.1.5.head: يَعرُب
67.1.5.meaning: Ya'rub ibn Qahtan, ancestor of the southern (Yemeni) Arabs, among them the poet's tribe of Azd.

68.2.1-5.meaning: “Dust in the mouth of whoever vies with you”: a curse meaning may he fail and be humbled. Afr and bara both mean earth, dust.

70.2.3.head: صَعَر
70.2.3.meaning: Sa'ar: the tilted cheek of pride.

71.2.1.head: أَفاوِق
71.2.1.meaning: Afawiq: the milk that gathers in the udder between milkings.

72.1.1.head: زالَ
72.1.1.meaning: Azalu: “I shall (not) cease”; the negative is dropped after an oath.

72.1.2.head: حَشو
72.1.2.meaning: Hashw: the filling, hence the wearer.

72.1.3.head: نَثرَة
72.1.3.meaning: Nathra: a long coat of mail.

72.2.5.meaning: Juthan: heaps of earth over a grave.

73.2.2-3.head: مَدَبّ النَّمل
73.2.2-3.meaning: “The track of ants”: the watered pattern of a fine blade, its wavy grain.

75.1.3.head: عَير
75.1.3.meaning: Ayr: the raised midrib of the blade.

78.1.1-2.head: مُشرِف الأَقطار
78.1.1-2.meaning: High in all his points: croup, head and withers.

78.2.1-2.meaning: With the last rib well raised; qusayra is the short rib at the back.

78.2.4-5.meaning: “Tight in the nasa”: the nasa is the sciatic vein running down the thigh; tautness there was prized.

79.1.4.head: القَطاة
79.1.4.meaning: Qata: the croup, where a second rider sits.

79.2.5.head: الصَّلا
79.2.5.meaning: Sala: the root of the tail.

80.2.5.meaning: Uja: the sinews at the back of the legs.

81.2.2.head: نُسور
81.2.2.meaning: Nusur: the frogs, the horny pads under the hoof.

82.2.5-6.head: نار الحُبا
82.2.5-6.meaning: Nar al-hubahib: sparks struck from stones by hooves, proverbially a fire that warms no one.

83.1.2.head: إِعليط
83.1.2.meaning: I'lit: the slender seed-pod of the markh shrub, likened to a horse's pricked ears.

84.1.4.head: شَجر
84.1.4.meaning: Shajr: the space between the jaws.

84.2.2.head: الصَّهوَة
84.2.2.meaning: Sahwa: the part of the back where the rider sits.

85.2.2.head: دَخيس
85.2.2.meaning: Dakhis: a swelling in the hoof.

85.2.5.meaning: Shaza: a splint, a bony growth on the foreleg.

86.1.2.head: اِعتَسَفَ
86.1.2.meaning: Struck out across, off the roads.

89.2.6.meaning: Glinted; the verb can also mean to hide.

92.1.3.head: رَحى
92.1.3.meaning: Raha: a millstone; here the thick of battle.

92.2.4-5.meaning: Qutb al-raha: the pivot of a millstone.

98.2.3.head: ثِغاب
98.2.3.meaning: Thighab: rainwater caught in hollows of rock.

99.2.5.meaning: Safa: the awns of grain, thorns.

100.1.2.head: الأَميران
100.1.2.meaning: The two emirs: the Mikalis who governed Fars, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Mikal and his son Abu al-Abbas Isma'il (al-Mas'udi); al-Lakhmi, from al-Qali, makes them brothers.

104.1.3.head: سَما
104.1.3.meaning: Raised: a dual verb, samawa, “the two of them raised”.

107.2.1.head: حَسوَة
107.2.1.meaning: Haswa: a single sip. “Like the” (kal) ends the first half: the word is split across the two halves, as both editions print it, for the metre.

108.1.2-3.head: اِبن ميكال
108.1.2-3.meaning: Ibn Mikal: the emir of Fars praised in the poem; Ibn Khalawayh calls him al-Shah ibn Mikal (shah is Persian for king).

109.1.2.head: ضَبع
109.1.2.meaning: “Took me by the upper arms”: raised me up, championed me.

109.1.3-4.head: أَبو العَبّاس
109.1.3-4.meaning: Abu al-Abbas: the second Mikali emir, Isma'il ibn Abd Allah ibn Mikal; al-Lakhmi makes him the Shah's brother.

109.2.3.head: الذَّرع
109.2.3.meaning: Dhar': reach, capacity; a narrow reach is helplessness.

112.1.6.head: مُعتَفي
112.1.6.meaning: One who comes seeking a gift.

112.2.2.head: أُوار
112.2.2.meaning: Uwar: burning heat; here of thirst.

120.2.1.head: النِّسرين
120.2.1.meaning: Nasrin: a white wild rose (eglantine), a Persian word.

121.1.3.head: الأَعصَم
121.1.3.meaning: A'sam: the ibex, the white-legged mountain goat.

124.1.2.head: الصَّهباء
124.1.2.meaning: Sahba': wine, named for its reddish colour.

124.2.6.meaning: Grew dark. Al-Lakhmi and Ibn Khalawayh read ghasa.

125.1.1.head: اِمتاحَ
125.1.1.meaning: Draws it up, as water from a well.

125.2.3.head: الظَّلم
125.2.3.meaning: Zalm: the sheen of the teeth.

125.2.5.head: اللَّمى
125.2.5.meaning: Lama: a darkish tint of the lips, prized by Arabs.

126.1.2.head: العَقيق
126.1.2.meaning: Al-Aqiq: a place near Basra (also the name of a valley near Medina).

126.1.3.head: الحَزيز
126.1.3.meaning: Al-Haziz: a place near Basra; properly stony ground.

126.1.4.head: المَلا
126.1.4.meaning: Al-Mala: a place near Basra; properly open country.

127.1.1.head: المِربَد
127.1.1.meaning: Al-Mirbad: the great market and meeting place of Basra, where poets recited; properly a camel pen.

128.1.3.head: مُقرَم
128.1.3.meaning: Muqram: a prize stallion camel kept for breeding; hence a chief.

131.1.1.head: جَون
131.1.1.meaning: Jawn: a dark rain-cloud (the word can also mean white).

132.1.2.head: يَمانٍ
132.1.2.meaning: From the south (the direction of Yemen).

132.2.3.head: كِسر
132.2.3.meaning: Kisr: the lower hem of a tent; here the cloud's lower edges.

136.1.4.meaning: Drove on with song, as camel-drivers do.

142.1.2.meaning: Jada: abundant rain; also a gift.

143.2.3-5.meaning: “The torrent has reached the lion-pits”: a proverb for a crisis past all bounds; lion-traps were dug on high ground.

145.1.1.head: نَهنَهَ
145.1.1.meaning: I curbed it, held it back.

146.2.3-6.meaning: “The caul has split in the belly”: a proverb for a case beyond remedy. The sala is the membrane round an unborn camel or lamb; if it tears inside, the young dies.

149.1.2.head: شَري
149.1.2.meaning: Shary: colocynth, a bitter desert gourd.

150.1.1.head: لَدن
150.1.1.meaning: Supple. Al-Lakhmi's text has layn, gentle.

150.2.1.meaning: Alwa: stubborn, unbending in a quarrel.

151.1.4.head: حِبوَة
151.1.4.meaning: Hibwa: a cloth an Arab sitting in council wrapped round his back and knees, a sign of composure.

153.2.1.head: أَشفى
153.2.1.meaning: They set me overlooking, as on a brink.

155.2.2.head: عِرض
155.2.2.meaning: Ird: honour, a man's good name.

155.2.5.meaning: Takha: a stain; properly the haze or thin cloud that darkens the sky.

156.2.5.head: اِنتَصى
156.2.5.meaning: And picked out as the best.

157.1.5.head: جُنَّة
157.1.5.meaning: Junna: a shield, anything that covers and protects.

159.2.5.meaning: Jana: fruit gathered from the tree.

160.2.6.meaning: Laha: the throat (plural of lahat, the uvula).

161.1.2.head: الشّارِخ
161.1.2.meaning: Sharikh: a youth in his prime.

162.2.3.head: التَّثقيف
162.2.3.meaning: Tathqif: truing a spear shaft over fire.

163.2.1.head: لَدن
163.2.1.meaning: Supple. Al-Lakhmi's reading; al-Harbi has ladnun.

165.2.4.head: أَنباث
165.2.4.meaning: Anbath: earth dug out of a well.

169.1.1.head: عاجَمَ
169.1.1.meaning: I have tested, as one bites a stick to try its hardness.

174.2.1.head: كَرَعَ
174.2.1.meaning: Laps, drinks with his mouth in the water like a beast.

174.2.6.meaning: Sara: water standing so long it has turned.

181.2.1.meaning: Mil'ib': “of the load”, min al-ib' run together.

185.1.4.head: شَطر
185.1.4.meaning: “Milked Time from both halves”: knew its good and bad; from milking a she-camel's teats two at a time.

186.1.1.head: فَرَّ
186.1.1.meaning: Has laid bare, as one opens a beast's mouth to tell its age; the subject is “my tooth”.

186.2.2.head: بازِل
186.2.2.meaning: Bazil: a camel in its ninth year, at full strength.

187.1.4.head: لَسَّ
187.1.4.meaning: Crops them, as a beast nibbles grass.

189.2.1.head: خابِط
189.2.1.meaning: One who beats trees to bring down leaves for fodder.

190.2.3.head: السّارِب
190.2.3.meaning: Sarib: one gone out to pasture; Ibn Khalawayh glosses it as the herdsman, then makes the grazing beast the image.

192.2.5-6.meaning: “That he had gone”: because he had gone.

199.1.2.head: اِحتازَ
199.1.2.meaning: Wins, takes possession of. Ibn Khalawayh's reading; both editions have yajtazu, passes beyond.

200.1.4.head: النَّدب
200.1.4.meaning: Nadb: quick to answer a call to honour.

215.1.3.head: هَدى
215.1.3.meaning: Guides, leads. Al-Lakhmi's text has tuhda, “is brought”.

217.2.4-5.meaning: “The end of the night march”, from the proverb “At dawn the travellers praise the night march”.

218.2.4.meaning: Jaba: the rim of a well.

219.2.4.head: اِمتَهى
219.2.4.meaning: To be tempered: steel was quenched in water to harden it.

221.2.5.meaning: Dawa: the puniness of a child born to close kin.

222.1.2-3.meaning: “His brother's daughter”: the lower fire-stick, cut from another branch of the same tree.

225.1.4.head: ريق
225.1.4.meaning: “The sun's spittle”: the heat-shimmer, like threads falling from the sky.

225.2.5.meaning: Cut to the pattern of the sandal: at noon the shadow lies under the foot.

226.1.1.head: طارِق
226.1.1.meaning: Tariq: one who comes by night.

228.2.1.head: زَفَّ
228.2.1.meaning: Leads it in, as a bride is led to her husband.

231.1.6.head: فارِس
231.1.6.meaning: Fars: the Persian province where Ibn Durayd lived with the Mikalis.

235.2.1-2.meaning: The Lord of the Throne: God.

238.1.2.meaning: Huliyya: “you dear ones there”, a diminutive of “you there”.

239.1.3-4.meaning: “The mother of the two boys”: a phrase in praise of a mature, perfect woman.

240.2.4.meaning: One led by the hand, like the blind.

242.2.1-2.meaning: “Daughter of eighty”: wine, either eighty years old or because drinkers were given eighty lashes.

253.2.4.head: رُوّاد
253.2.4.meaning: Ruwwad: scouts sent ahead in search of pasture.
